spans.text: Chazal structured the evening Shema by having us say two brachos before we say the Shema, and two brachos afterward. Then we will be ready for our one-on-one with Hashem—the Shemoneh Esrei.

Hashem Created the Cycle of Day and Night

spans.text: מַעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים

You—בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה Hashem, are the Source of everything; You—אֱלֹהֵינוּ take care of us; מֶלֶךְ—and You rule the entire world; אֲשֶׁר בִּדְבָרוֹ—simply by His Word, evening begins. And with His wisdom He created the seasons, constellations of stars, and night and day. אֵל חַי—וְקַיָּם May Hashem, Who is eternal and never-changing, תָּמִיד יִמְלוֹךְ עָלֵינוּ לְעוֹלָם—rule over us continuously forever. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הַמַּעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים—Who brings on evenings.

Your—אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל love for Your people, Bnei Yisrael, is eternal! (And a sign of that love is that) You taught us Your Torah and gave us Your mitzvos. Therefore, we always study Your Torah, day and

night, and are so happy to be learning Torah and fulfilling Your mitzvos! For they are the essence of our life and what keeps us going. וְאַהֲבָתְךָ אַל תָּסִיר מִמֶּנּוּ—Please do not remove Your love from us, ever!
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; אוֹהֵב עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל—Who (no matter what) loves His nation, Yisrael.

שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל—As a proud member of Bnei Yisrael, I publicly proclaim; that יְהֹוָה—the Eternal God, Who always was, is, and will be; אֱלֹהֵינוּ—I accept as our personal, all-powerful God (with all the responsibilities that come with that!); יְהֹוָה—and that God, Who controls all aspects of my life and of the universe; is אֶחָד—the One and Only controlling power.

שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל—As a proud member of Bnei Yisrael, I publicly proclaim; that יְהֹוָה—the Name that represents God's attribute of mercy; אֱלֹהֵינוּ—is the same God as Elokim, the Name that represents His attribute of strict judgment. יְהֹוָה אֶחָד—It is all the same God. And all is merciful, since all that He does is for our good (just that sometimes the "medicine" is bitter).
בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ—May the perception of Hashem's Presence and rulership be increased (so all humans will recognize His existence and power); לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—forever and ever.
Next, the Torah describes the obligation of each individual:

And—וְאָהַבְתָּ אֶת יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ you must love Hashem with your whole heart; וּבְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ וּבְכָל—and dedicate all your talents, your unique personality, all your character traits, and all that He has given you (to His service), out of a sense of gratitude and love. וְהָיוּ הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ—And Torah and mitzvos should (not be external and mechanical, but rather) be from your heart; וְשִׁנַּנְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם (and they should be so dear to you that) you pass it on to your children, and it is what you constantly talk about; בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ—wherever you are, all the time. וּקְשַׁרְתָּם לְאוֹת עַל יָדֶךָ וְהָיוּ לְטֹטָפֹת בֵּין עֵינֶיךָ—You should dedicate your actions and thoughts to Hashem, symbolized by putting tefillin on your arm and on your head; וּכְתַבְתָּם עַל—מְזוּזֹת בֵּיתֶךָ וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ—and your entire home should be dedicated to Him, symbolized by putting mezuzos on your doorposts.

וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ—If you, Bnei Yisrael, will listen intently and follow My commandments, to love Hashem and serve Him to the best of your ability with a full heart, then I will provide you with your material needs, and you will be satisfied. הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם פֶּן יִפְתֶּה לְבַבְכֶם—But be careful! That material wealth may go to your head and lead you astray and corrupt your value system, and you will "worship other gods." You may come to think that it is money, power, and prestige that control your future. (Then, in order to help you return to clarity,) וְחָרָה אַף Hashem—יְהוָה בָּכֶם וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם will take away all that material wealth; and He will send you, Am Yisrael, out of Eretz Yisrael. (But even in exile,) וּקְשַׁרְתֶּם אֹתָם לְאוֹת עַל you—יֶדְכֶם וְהָיוּ לְטוֹטָפֹת בֵּין עֵינֵיכֶם should dedicate your actions and thoughts to Hashem, symbolized by putting tefillin on your arm and

וּלְמַדְתֶּם אֹתָם אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם on your head. וּלְמַדְתֶּם בָּם—And you should teach Torah to your children so that they speak about (and apply) Torah; בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ

וּבְקוּמֶךָ—And your entire home should be dedicated to Him, symbolized by putting mezuzos on your doorposts. לְמַעַן יִרְבּוּ יְמֵיכֶם—That will ensure that Bnei Yisrael will return to the Land that Hashem promised our ancestors.

וַיֹּאמֶר—Moshe was told by Hashem to tell Bnei Yisrael: You must place tzitzis at the edges of your four-cornered garments and put on each corner one techeiles-colored string. וּרְאִיתֶם אוֹתוֹ—By looking at it (techeiles is the color of the sea, which is similar to the sky, which looks like a sapphire, which will remind you of the throne of Hashem—a lesson that spiritual growth is a slow, step-by-step process!) you will think about the mitzvos and do them. וְלֹא תָתֻרוּ אַחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם—Do not be swayed by the temptations or doubts that arise in your heart, or by immoral thoughts that are triggered by watching things one should not be watching! לְמַעַן תִּזְכְּרוּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת

כָּל מִצְוֹתַי—Be constantly aware of what is proper, and fulfill all My mitzvos; וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים לֵאלֹהֵיכֶם—and this will elevate and sanctify your life. I am Hashem, Who takes care of you and miraculously took you out of Egypt to be your personal God. אֲנִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם—I (the same God Who did all those public, overt miracles in Egypt) am Your God now (even though at times My Presence is hidden); אֱמֶת—and that is the truth!
וֶאֱמוּנָה כָּל זֹאת—We are absolutely certain that Hashem alone is our personal God, and we are His

people (with all the responsibilities and rewards that come with that!). Hashem demonstrates this constantly by saving us from our enemies; protecting us from those who wish to destroy us physically and spiritually; and ensuring our survival with great miracles. He took us out of Egypt with great miracles and drowned the Egyptians at the Yam Suf. At that time, all Bnei Yisrael saw Your power, accepted You as King, and Moshe and Bnei Yisrael sang Your praises with great joy and called out:
Among all the powers (powers of nature, powers of humans), who is equal to You, Who is like You, powerful but with purity of purpose?
When You split the sea, Bnei Yisrael saw Your majesty and exclaimed: זֶה אֵלִי—"This is my God!" and they said:
(Just as we have seen the rulership of Hashem here at the sea, so too for all future times) Hashem will reign forever and ever!

As the pasuk clearly says: "Hashem has redeemed Yaakov and rescued him from those stronger than him." בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; גָּאַל יִשְׂרָאֵל—Who redeemed Bnei Yisrael.

הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ—May we rest peacefully tonight and wake up refreshed and full of life tomorrow. Give us the ability to make clear and good choices; וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ—protect us from dangers; לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ—so that we can fulfill our mission on this world and make a kiddush Hashem! Save us from wars, famine, and sickness; וְהָסֵר שָׂטָן מִלְּפָנֵינוּ—and remove the Satan from in front of us and from behind us (see Instant Insight). And please personally shelter us from all evil, for You are our Protector Who constantly saves us, for You are a merciful and compassionate King. וּשְׁמוֹר צֵאתֵנוּ וּבוֹאֵנוּ—Guard all our comings and goings; לְחַיִּים וּלְשָׁלוֹם—that we should live, and be at peace; בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, now and forever! מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם—Who protects שׁוֹמֵר עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַד—His nation Bnei Yisrael forever!

בָּרוּךְ יְהוָה לְעוֹלָם אָמֵן וְאָמֵן—It is the absolute truth that Hashem is the Source of everything! He protects Eretz Yisrael, Yerushalayim, and Bnei Yisrael, and someday the entire world will recognize His

Presence. Hashem will never abandon His people, and we put our complete trust in Hashem. The time will come when all the nations of the world will come and bow to Hashem! בָּרוּךְ יְהוָה I thank Hashem—בַּיּוֹם, בָּרוּךְ יְהוָה בַּלַּיְלָה for all that He does for me during the day (when I can see His kindness) and for all He does for me during the night (when it is hard to see His kindness). Hashem, I put myself in Your Hands at all times! May we soon rejoice with the coming of Mashiach, when You will rule forever over the whole world. Because You are—כִּי הַמַּלְכוּת הִיא the only true King; וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עַד תִּמְלֹךְ and You rule over everything—בִּכְבוֹד for we—כִּי אֵין לָנוּ מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא אַתָּה ,forever have no other King but You! בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה You, Hashem, are the Source of—יְהוָה everything; הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּכְבוֹדוֹ תָּמִיד יִמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ Who personally—לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד וְעַל כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו rules (specifically) over us (His people) and over all mankind forever!

Important Instant Insight: The idea of a "yoke" in the concept of עול מלכות שמים—accepting the yoke of kingdom of Heaven" seems to carry an image of mitzvos being a heavy and difficult burden that we shlep around on our backs our whole life. But that is the superficial understanding. True, at times mitzvos seem "heavy" and difficult, and we are obligated to persevere, but the choice of the term "עול—yoke" carries a profound message. As I heard from Rav Matisyahu Solomon, shlita, a yoke is simply a tool that allows the animal to do its job in the most efficient and easy way possible. How else could it pull the wagon if it did not have a yoke? So, too, when we proclaim the Shema and publicly accept עול מלכות שמים, we must realize that the mitzvos are perfectly crafted, precise tools that allow us to do OUR job here on earth! How would we manage without them?

Instant Insight: The letters of the word ש-מ-ע are the same as the letters that begin the words עול מלכות שמים but backwards! The message is that even when Torah laws and values seem "backwards" to us—as if they make no sense—nevertheless, we accept that in truth they are the tools for our success.

Instant Insight: In the Torah, the pasuk of the Shema has the letters ע and ד (which spell עד—witness) enlarged. The very miracle of our survival—that after all these years Jews all over the world are united in their proclamation of the Shema—is itself witness to the truth of the Torah!

spans.text: הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ

Important Instant Insight:
וְהָסֵר שָׂטָן מִלְּפָנֵינוּ וּמֵאַחֲרֵינוּ—Remove the Satan from in front of us and from behind us." The Satan "in front of us" is clear: it is the click on the mouse we shouldn't make, the outfit that's only appropriate if we don't breathe or move, the funny story about someone we shouldn't say, and the not-so-kosher business deal we should turn down. But what is the Satan "behind us"? That is our past: those mistakes we made and our insecurities that are now whispering in our ear, "Who do you think you are anyway? You're not so frum! That next step of growth isn't for guys like you—just give it up!" All of this is false, as our mistakes in the past do not prevent our future growth! We therefore ask Hashem to help us overcome the "Satan of the past" so we can continue conquering new levels of growth.
